title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's combinatorial study of a curve X given as a cover of P^1 branched only over 0, 1 and ∞, that is, a dessin d'enfant.

- X is triangulated by the preimages of the two half-planes. The set of triangles (flags) is R.
- R carries three involutions τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞. Each τ_i reflects a triangle across its side opposite the vertex of type i. These generate the cartographic group.
- S = S_0 ⊔ S_1 ⊔ S_∞ is the set of vertices.
- X̃^{*an} is X with small open discs around all vertices removed, so a compact surface with boundary.
- One studies its fundamental groupoid based at a finite set of points R_r^{ij}. These sit on the side ij of triangle r, near the vertex of type i, on the boundary of the small disc.

What the page does. It first summarises the previous pages: 4 = 1+3 presentations of Π_1(X̃^{*an}, base points). There is one 'symmetric' presentation using all paths (8) and (9). There are three more obtained by eliminating, for a fixed type i, the paths a_r^i and the base points lying on them.

It then treats a more drastic reduction. One keeps only the paths a_r^∞, i.e. the transverse arcs of a single type. The new base set (17) is {R_r^{ij} : r ∈ R, {i,j} = {0,1}}, the points on the 0–1 edges near the 0-end and the 1-end. They are identified across the edge by R_r^{ij} = R_{τ_∞ r}^{ij}.

The generators (18) are:
- a_r^∞ : R_r^{01} → R_r^{10}, running along the 0–1 edge (one per edge, after the τ_∞ identification);
- Λ_r^0 : R_r^{01} → R_{τ_1 r}^{01}, an arc of the small circle around the type-0 vertex;
- Λ_r^{11} : R_r^{10} → R_{τ_0 r}^{10}, an arc of the small circle around the type-1 vertex.

The only relations (19) are redundancy relations Λ_r^0 Λ_{τ_1 r}^0 = 1 and Λ_r^{11} Λ_{τ_0 r}^{11} = 1. These just say that the arc traversed from the neighbouring triangle is the inverse arc, since τ_0 and τ_1 are involutions.

So the groupoid is directly exhibited as free. Geometrically, X̃^{*an} deformation-retracts onto the 'fattened dessin': the bipartite graph (black vertices type 0, white type 1, edges = 0–1 segments) with each vertex replaced by a small circle. The faces of the complement are the polygons centred at the type-∞ points, which the figure draws 'with rounded corners to avoid the holes'. Choosing which type of vertex plays the role of face centre gives three such presentations, based at S∖S_i, for i = ∞ (worked out), 0 or 1.

The next page carries out a further reduction (base points R_r^{01} only, with composite paths A_r^{01}). It announces 10 = 1+3+3+3 presentations in total, followed by the 'bouchage des trous', i.e. filling the discs back in to get presentations of Π_1(X) and of the punctured curves.

Purpose. These are explicit combinatorial presentations of the profinite or discrete fundamental groupoid of the dessin's surface, in terms of the cartographic-group data (R, τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞). They serve the programme of making the Galois action on Teichmüller-type towers explicit via the combinatorics of dessins.
errors: No mathematical error. The construction is the standard retraction of a punctured surface onto a fattened ribbon graph. The relations are only inverse/redundancy relations, so freeness is correct.
Minor notational slip on the page: the second redundancy line is written R_r^{1,0} = R_{τ_∞(r)}, missing the superscript 1,0.
The labelling of the second family of circle arcs is inconsistent: Λ'^1_r in the text versus Λ_r^{11} and Λ_r^{10} in the figure.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of a surface with holes based at a finite, combinatorially defined set of base points, presented as a free groupoid on arcs of a fattened graph
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid on a set of base points; ribbon graph / fat graph spine of a punctured surface
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brown (groupoids with several base points); Penner, Harer, Kontsevich (fat graphs); Grothendieck (Esquisse) for the systematic use of many base points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3: groupoïdes fondamentaux basés en des ensembles de points, dessins/cartes; La Longue Marche (1981) contains related material

ideas.what: Description of a dessin via the triangle set R with three involutions τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞ (cartographic group), and presentations of π_1 derived from it
ideas.modern_name: Cartographic group (Grothendieck's group of maps), flag/triangle description of dessins
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); developed by Jones–Singerman, Malgoire–Voisin, Shabat–Voevodsky
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §3 (cartographic group C_2 and its quotient)

ideas.what: Systematic enumeration of 10 = 1+3+3+3 equivalent presentations, according to which vertex types are eliminated or chosen as face centres
ideas.modern_name: Choice of spine / duality among the three vertex types of a dessin (bipartite map vs. its duals)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in dessin theory (symmetry under S_3 permuting 0, 1, ∞)

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping of standard presentations of the fundamental groupoid of a punctured surface carried by a dessin. It is correct but routine and consistent with ideas Grothendieck published in the Esquisse; nothing here appears new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the space is Π_1(X̃^{*an}, S) (the 'an' superscript), as in the next page's X̃^{^an}.
'le cas où on élimine deux côtés des triangles fondamentaux' — 'la cas' should be 'le cas'.
'ce qui conduit ainsi' is probably 'ce qui revient ainsi' or 'ce qui conduit à ceci'.
The second circle-arc generator appears in the figure as Λ_r^{11} (and the other as Λ_r^{10}), not Λ_r^{'1}.
Redundancy relation should read R_r^{1,0} = R^{1,0}_{τ_∞(r)}.
Final line: 'Π_1(X̃^{*an}, S∖S_i), pour i = ∞ [cas explicité] ou 0 ou 1'.
'R_φ' near 'cst. S' is likely R_s (s ∈ S), consistent with the next page's R_{φ s}.
